metaphor: the redline: an insurer's typeset denial letter marked up by hand in a litigator's ink by someone on the patient's side; the gate is a signature line
category_convention_avoided: insurtech/legal-tech SaaS: white or navy, blue accent, progress stepper, rounded cards, chat bubble; health adds calming teal
design_code: Marks are drawn and animate on, because a person is marking this up, not a pipeline.
The letter is set in the insurer's own boring type, because it is theirs and should look like it.
UI chrome is Atkinson Hyperlegible, because it was designed for low-vision readers and the person reading this is sick.
The canvas is paper, because a dark default would misrepresent the material; the ledger's last seven entries are dark, so light is the anti-convergent choice.
expressive_axis: the marks: hand-drawn oxblood ink, animated on, everything else quiet

canvas.override_reason: The artifact is a paper letter and the work is ink on it. Dark would lie about the material. Seven consecutive dark entries in the ledger make light the differentiating choice now.

dark.note: At night the room is dark and the paper is still paper. Only the desk changes; contrast on the sheet is verified separately.

type.voice: a typed form letter, marked up by a steady hand

structure: sheet-with-margin: letter column left, annotation margin right, second sheet below for the appeal, signature line as the gate

edge_depth.marks: SVG strokes with slight roughness, no blur

motion.explains: that a person is working through the letter in order
motion.signature: the deadline date is circled, then an arrow is drawn to the margin where day 30 and the six-month count are written by hand

headline_numbers: the statutory deadline, circled, with the count from day 30 written beside it
the published overturn rate for this cohort, with its scope in words and the count behind it
